cards.title: Zelenskyy details rift with dismissed defence minister
cards.summary: AP reported Zelenskyy publicly describing his dispute with dismissed defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov while also discussing battlefield pressure and peace talks.
detail: The Associated Press reported that President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said actions by dismissed defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov, including involvement in protests and calls for an election, were misguided. Zelenskyy also discussed battlefield developments, ballistic-missile defence, negotiations and Ukraine’s budget pressures.

The significance is institutional as well as military: a public dispute at the top of the defence apparatus arrives while Ukraine is describing pressure from Russian attacks and continuing its own long-range operations. AP reported Zelenskyy’s claims; they are not an independent finding about the dispute.

The next reliable checks are an official account of the ministry transition, any further evidence about the alleged protests, and measurable movement in negotiations. Battlefield claims and the timing of any promised operations remain attributed and uncertain.

cards.summary: Official Gamescom pages list gamescom dev in Cologne from Aug. 23–25, followed by the wider gamescom event Aug. 26–30 and Opening Night Live on Aug. 25.
detail: The official Gamescom dev conference page lists the developer event for Aug. 23–25, 2026 in Cologne. Gamescom’s main site lists the public event for Aug. 26–30 and identifies Opening Night Live on Aug. 25 as the week’s opening broadcast.

For European game watchers, the sequence separates the professional developer programme from the public trade-fair and livestream schedule. The official site also highlights indie, accessibility and industry programming, but programme details can change as organisers update the calendar.
The next check is the official livestream timetable and venue access information before each day. This card is an upcoming event listing, not a claim about announcements that have not yet happened.
cards.why: It is the clearest current EU-wide games event with verified dates and both professional and public tracks.
verifiedFacts: Gamescom’s official information lists Opening Night Live on Aug. 25.
The public Gamescom event is scheduled for Cologne later that week.
analysis: The event has separate public, business, and showcase windows that should not be collapsed into one timetable.
uncertainty: Final programme details and access information may change before the show.

cards.title: U.S. futures ease as Iran sanctions and Nvidia stay in focus
cards.summary: Reuters reported S&P 500 futures down 0.1% and Nasdaq futures down 0.4% early Monday as investors awaited Iran sanctions details and Nvidia results.
detail: Reuters reported that S&P 500 futures were down 0.1% and Nasdaq futures 0.4% in early Monday trading. The same report said investors were watching threatened U.S. sanctions on Iran, Nvidia’s Wednesday results and Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s upcoming remarks.

The useful distinction is between the observed futures move and the drivers being watched: the market snapshot is time-stamped, while the sanctions response, earnings outcome and rate expectations remained open. Reuters also reported a 5.2518% 30-year Treasury yield in the checked frame.
The next update should replace futures with the relevant cash-session close and refresh the policy and earnings signals. This card is descriptive and contains no investment recommendation.

cards.title: Oil gives back part of last week’s Iran premium
cards.summary: Reuters put Brent at $93.07 and U.S. crude at $85.64 in early Monday trading, both lower before the U.S. sanctions briefing.
detail: In the Reuters snapshot, Brent crude was down 1.4% at $93.07 and U.S. crude down 1.6% at $85.64. The report noted that the move followed a 6.6% Brent gain the previous week and came before a U.S. briefing on sanctions against Iran.

The market signal is therefore a change in the session, not evidence that the geopolitical risk has disappeared. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, the sanctions design and any response from Iran remain the variables most likely to change the energy picture.
The next check is the official settlement and any confirmed policy announcement. Prices are volatile and this card is informational only.

cards.title: European shares head into a weekly loss as yields stay elevated
cards.summary: European benchmarks were broadly steady or firmer on Friday, but the week remained negative as borrowing costs and oil weighed on sentiment.
detail: Reuters and AP both described a steadier Friday session alongside a difficult week for markets. AP reported gains in much of Europe and Asia, while Reuters linked the broader weekly loss to fluctuating bond yields and higher oil.

The market signal is therefore a session rebound inside a more defensive weekly backdrop. Higher long-term yields matter because they raise financing costs and compete with equities for investors’ attention.
The next session will bring fresh price discovery after the weekend. The figures are descriptive and time-stamped, not forecasts.

cards.title: Asian shares slip ahead of Iran sanctions details
cards.summary: Reuters reported lower Asian equities, with the Nikkei down 0.5%, South Korea down 2.8% and China blue chips down 1.2% in the early session.
detail: Reuters reported that Asian share markets slipped on Monday while investors awaited details of threatened U.S. sanctions on Iran. It cited a 0.5% fall in the Nikkei, a 2.8% fall in South Korean shares, a 0.5% fall in Taiwan and a 1.2% drop in Chinese blue chips.

The regional driver is a mix of geopolitical risk and technology expectations: the report also said Nvidia results were weighing on the tech sector and that oil had eased ahead of the sanctions announcement. These are market observations, not forecasts.
The next check is the close across the named markets and the formal sanctions announcement. The time-zone gap means this Asia card can change before the U.S. session begins.
